details: Bitcoin climbed above $61,000, setting up for a weekly gain after softer-than-expected U.S. jobs data reduced fears of Federal Reserve interest rate hikes. This positive macroeconomic sentiment was coupled with US spot Bitcoin ETFs recording $221.7 million in net inflows on Thursday, marking the strongest single-day intake since early May and ending a 10-day outflow streak.
title: Bitcoin Surges Past $61K on ETF Inflows, Eased Rate Fears

details: Ethereum experienced a significant short squeeze, leading to $160.8 million in futures positions being liquidated. The price gained over 5% in the past day, driven by this short squeeze and expanding institutional access through integrations like Anchorage Digital's Lido, which now offers direct access to staked ETH.
title: Ethereum Short Squeeze Propels Price Amid Institutional Interest

details: Robinhood's newly launched layer-2 blockchain, Robinhood Chain, has designated Uniswap (UNI) as its primary Automated Market Maker (AMM). This significant DeFi-TradFi integration is expected to provide UNI with exposure to Robinhood's large retail user base, contributing to an over 11% gain for UNI.
title: Robinhood Chain Picks Uniswap as Primary Automated Market Maker

details: Japanese investment firm Metaplanet acquired an additional 2,823 Bitcoins for $225 million in Q2 2026, increasing its total treasury holdings to 43,000 BTC. This strategic move reinforces institutional confidence and ongoing accumulation of Bitcoin.
title: Metaplanet Boosts Bitcoin Holdings with New $225M Purchase

details: Standard Chartered has become the first global systematically important bank (G-SIB) to offer direct stablecoin services, enabling institutional clients to mint and redeem USDC directly through its banking platform. This streamlines access for institutions, potentially increasing adoption and liquidity in the stablecoin market.
title: Standard Chartered Becomes First Major Bank to Offer Direct Stablecoin Services

details: The broader cryptocurrency market recorded approximately $554 million in liquidations over the past 24 hours. Short positions accounted for the majority, with around $390 million, while Ethereum and Bitcoin related liquidations stood at $219 million and $122 million, respectively.
title: Crypto Market Sees $554 Million in Liquidations Over 24 Hours
